summary: Dominica’s pledges mix forest conservation, restoration and agricultural transformation. Conservation targets 65% protected forest—about 471.9 km² if applied to the current 726 km² (96.2%) forest area—and REDD+ sequestration of 648 Gg annually in 2020–2025 and 621 Gg in 2025–2030; passages report differing annual figures of about 100 Gg and 600+ Gg. Restoration sets 6,995 Gg CO2e sequestration by 2030, a reported 980% increase above 2018, improvement of 20% of degraded land, 25% higher healthy coral reef cover and one million trees. Mixed measures rehabilitate 75% of degraded land in Saint Andrew plus 100 km² elsewhere by 2030, and restore 25% of degraded areas with 100 km² of sustainable cropland and agroforestry. A 100 km² component equals 13.2% of the 755 km² land area. Agriculture targets 50% increases in agroforestry farming and farmer numbers, 50% lower emissions, 20% productivity/SOC gains, 50% tree crops on sloped land and 40% organic cultivation.
